newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks to raise prices again.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks to raise prices again.

text.p: Upscale coffee retailer Starbucks Corp. plans to raise prices again on Friday to reflect higher coffee futures prices.

According to store managers, Starbucks plans to raise beverage prices by five cents a cup, bringing the cost of a tall coffee in some retail outlets to $1.25. Whole bean prices are also expected to rise.
The increase is the second time Seattle-based Starbucks has raised prices this year. In March, it raised beverage prices by five cents a cup and bean prices by 30 cents a pound.
Coffee futures prices hit a new 20-year record in New York Wednesday on jitters about cold weather in Brazil at a time when stocks are already low and supply is tight from Latin America.
At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, futures for arabica coffee beans for July delivery rose almost seven cents to $2.81 per pound, the highest in two decades.

Forecasts for cool winter weather in Brazil, the biggest exporter, did not point to a damaging frost. But they were enough to trigger new speculative buying in a rally that has lifted prices for American arabica coffees by 150 percent this year.

Less-prized robustas, from Africa and Asia, are in better supply. But the benchmark London July robusta contract was also higher on Wednesday and, at just below $2,200, was firmer by about 80 percent since January 1.
A spokesman for Starbucks was not immediately available for comment.
